draft.title: Parallel structure
card: Parallel structure means using the same grammatical pattern for each item in a list or each part of a pair. For example: "She likes to swim, to run and to climb."
Each part has the same form, such as all -ing words, all "to" verbs, or all short clauses built the same way. A part that breaks the pattern sounds clumsy.
Faulty: "He enjoys hiking, swimming and to cycle." Fixed: "He enjoys hiking, swimming and cycling."
Effect: the repeated pattern gives balance and rhythm. It also makes ideas easy to compare, because the reader sees each part lined up beside the next.
draft.remember: Keep the same pattern for each part. The repeat gives balance and makes comparing easy.

opts: Lena packed her boots, her jacket and her torch
Lena packed her boots, her jacket and took a torch
Lena packed her boots, a jacket and to take a torch
Lena packed her boots, bringing her jacket and a torch
a.why: All three items in the right answer are noun phrases built the same way: her plus a noun. The other options switch between nouns and verbs, which breaks the pattern, so the list sounds uneven.
a.clue: Check that every item in the list has the same form.

b.q: A speaker says, "We came to the dam to swim, to fish, and wanting quiet." Which rewrite fixes the pattern?
opts: We came to the dam to swim, to fish and to rest
We came to the dam to swim, fishing and to rest
We came to the dam to swim, to fish and for quiet
We came to the dam to swim, to fish and resting
b.why: The fixed version repeats "to" plus a verb for all three items, so the list is balanced. The option ending "for quiet" looks close, but it swaps a verb pattern for a noun phrase, so the pattern still breaks.
b.clue: Match the form of the first two items exactly.
